description: We are a group of engineers and physicists (100% STEM!) united by a single great passion: space exploration. We are ready to tackle this experience and are always open to exchanging ideas, networking, and connecting with other participants!
summary:
This project aims to create a unified environment for astronauts, Mission Control, and scientists. While each group has a distinct role, they will all rely on the same daily-synchronized data. This shared access is crucial for human space exploration: it optimizes both technological and scientific planning and, most importantly, ensures astronaut safety.

Today, the maps we use to plan surface operations come from orbit. They are global, but they lack resolution—a single rock outcrop can easily be smaller than one pixel.

A mission is designed on Earth long before launch. First, we set the global exploration goals. Then, in the strategic phase, we turn orbital maps into a baseline plan. But true ground truth only arrives after landing, in the day-to-day tactical phase on site. This is the precise operational gap that SyncroWalk fills.

Every Sol follows the same four-step loop. Astronauts and the hub gather data. The map updates, shrinking uncertainty along the paths we’ve walked. Scientists then re-prioritize their targets. Finally, Mission Control safely re-plans the next steps—checking radiation doses, walk-back times, and terrain—before approving the plan. Then, the cycle repeats.

SyncroWalk connects three key roles on one shared map: scientists decide what to explore, Mission Control decides how to get there safely, and astronauts execute and provide feedback. Every decision is sequential, tracked, and approved.
details:
SyncroWalk is a collaborative Mars EVA planning app for the first human missions to Mars. It gives three roles the same mission map and state: the Scientist defines targets and hypotheses, Mission Control plans routes and checks safety, and the Astronaut follows the approved EVA and submits the debrief. The app uses real NASA orbital data from Jezero Crater and runs workflow checks such as GO / NO-GO safety validation before a plan can be sent.


It works by keeping one shared map and one mission model, then applying safety rules to each route: duration, return buffer, slope, shelter time, suit consumables, terrain quality, radiation dose, and SEP alerts. If a plan fails, it can be re-planned before being approved.


Benefits:
•⁠ ⁠Faster and better mission coordination
•⁠ ⁠Safer EVA planning with built-in constraint checks
•⁠ ⁠Shared decision-making across roles
•⁠ ⁠Clear evidence trail for every plan, review, and replan


Intended impact:
•⁠ ⁠Improve planning for future human exploration on Mars
•⁠ ⁠Reduce risk and delays in EVA operations
•⁠ ⁠Help mission teams use real data and structured decision-making before sending astronauts onto the surface


Tools and stack:
•⁠ ⁠React 19
•⁠ ⁠TypeScript
•⁠ ⁠Vite
•⁠ ⁠Leaflet
•⁠ ⁠NASA Mars Trek / CRISM / THEMIS / Perseverance MMGIS data
•⁠ ⁠Node.js + npm
•⁠ ⁠Browser localStorage for persistent mission state
•⁠ ⁠No dedicated hardware required; this is a web application


Why it’s creative:
•⁠ ⁠It combines real scientific Mars data with a mission-planning simulation
•⁠ ⁠It turns complex exploration tasks into a role-based collaborative interface
•⁠ ⁠It adds a realistic “planning loop” from science objective to EVA execution and debrief


Key factors the team considered:
•⁠ ⁠Crew safety and survivability
•⁠ ⁠Radiation and environmental risk
•⁠ ⁠Terrain and mobility constraints
•⁠ ⁠Time and resource limits
•⁠ ⁠Data uncertainty and mission realism
•⁠ ⁠Clear collaboration between science, operations, and field crew


In short, SyncroWalk is a mission-planning tool that makes Mars surface exploration more coordinated, safer, and more realistic for future crewed missions
